Rashi on Shabbat 107a:1:1.hebrew: תחת כנפיו - תחת כנפי כסותו, ואין יכול לצאת, שננעל בפניו מאליו:
Rashi on Shabbat 107a:1:1.english: Under his flaps - Under the flaps of his garment, and [the bird] cannot get out, for it was shut in on its own.

Rashi on Shabbat 107a:1:2.hebrew: יושב ומשמרו - כן, ואינו צריך לפתוח לו חלון, דאינו אלא שומר:
Rashi on Shabbat 107a:1:2.english: He sits and guards it - [He may do] so, and he does not need to open a window for it, for he is merely guarding [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 107a:1:3.english: To one who locks his house - For all people do so.

Rashi on Shabbat 107a:3:1.english: One who drains - [One who] lances an abscess, [in Old French:] *coiture*.

Rashi on Shabbat 107a:3:10.hebrew: על עקרב שלא תשוך - ואע"ג דממילא מתציד:
Rashi on Shabbat 107a:3:10.english: On top of a scorpion so it will not bite - Even though it is trapped incidentally.

Rashi on Shabbat 107a:3:2.hebrew: אם לעשות לה פה - בתוספתא תני הכי: אם לקולפה ולעשות לה פה, כדרך שרופאים של עכשיו עושין, דמתקן לה פתח:
Rashi on Shabbat 107a:3:2.english: If [he did so] to make an opening for it - In the Tosefta it is taught thus: "If [he did so] to peel it and make an opening for it," in the manner that present-day physicians do, for he fashions an opening for it.

Rashi on Shabbat 107a:3:3.hebrew: חייב - משום בונה פתח, או משום מתקן כלי; מה לי לתקן מכה, מה לי לתקן כלי:
Rashi on Shabbat 107a:3:3.english: He is liable - Because of building an opening, or because of repairing a utensil; what is the difference to me [between] repairing a wound [and] repairing a utensil?

Rashi on Shabbat 107a:3:4.hebrew: ואם להוציא לחה - של עכשיו, ואינו חושש אם תחזור ותסתום מיד:
Rashi on Shabbat 107a:3:4.english: And if [it is] to drain fluid - [that is there] now, and he is not concerned if it closes up again immediately.

Rashi on Shabbat 107a:3:5.hebrew: פטור - ומותר, דאין כאן תיקון, ורבנן נמי לא גזור בה שבות משום צערא:
Rashi on Shabbat 107a:3:5.english: He is exempt - and [it is] permitted, for there is no repair here, and the Rabbis also did not decree a shevut [rabbinic prohibition] on it because of [the] pain.

Rashi on Shabbat 107a:3:6.english: And a hand needle - [may be] moved on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 107a:3:7.hebrew: ליטול בה את הקוץ - והיינו דומיא דלחה, דמצער ליה ואינו חושש אם יסתם מיד, וקאמר ניטלת לכתחילה. מחט של יד, היא מחט שתופרין בה בגדים, ומשום דקתני בהדה "ושל שק לפתוח בה את הדלת", קרי לה להאי "מחט של יד":
Rashi on Shabbat 107a:3:7.english: To remove a thorn with it - And this is similar to [draining] fluid, for it pains him and he does not care if [the wound] closes immediately, and [the Mishnah] says [the needle] may be taken ab initio. "A hand needle" is a needle with which one sews garments, and because it teaches alongside it, "and [a needle] for sackcloth, to open a door with it," it calls this one "a hand needle."

Rashi on Shabbat 107a:3:9.hebrew: כופין - לכתחילה, ולא שיכבה את הנר. ואשמעינן דכלי ניטל להצלת דבר שאינו ניטל בשבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 107a:3:9.english: One may overturn [a bowl] - [This is permitted] ab initio, provided he does not extinguish the lamp. And [the Mishnah] teaches us that a utensil may be moved to save something that may not be moved on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 107a:5:1.english: Eight creeping animals - The weasel and the mouse, etc. (Leviticus 11).

Rashi on Shabbat 107a:5:2.english: One who traps them - [he is] liable, because its species is trapped.

Rashi on Shabbat 107a:5:3.hebrew: והחובל בהן חייב - דיש להן עור, כדמפרש בגמרא, והויא ליה חבורה שאינה חוזרת, והויא ליה תולדה דשוחט. לוי"ה. ל"א: כיון דיש להן עור, נצבע העור בדם הנצרר בו, דחייב משום צובע:
Rashi on Shabbat 107a:5:3.english: And one who wounds them is liable - Because they have a hide, as [the Gemara] explains, and it is a wound that does not return [to its former state], and it is a derivative [forbidden labor] of slaughtering. Leviyah. Another version: Since they have a hide, the hide is dyed by the blood that collects in it, so that one is liable on account of dyeing.

Rashi on Shabbat 107a:5:4.english: And other abominations and crawling things - Such as worms, snakes, and scorpions.

Rashi on Shabbat 107a:5:5.english: One who wounds them is exempt - Because they have no skin.

Rashi on Shabbat 107a:5:6.hebrew: שלא לצורך פטור - דאין במינו ניצוד, והויא מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה, ור' שמעון היא, כדמוקי לה בגמ':
Rashi on Shabbat 107a:5:6.english: For no [specific] need [he is] exempt - For its species is not [ordinarily] trapped, and [thus] it is a labor not needed for its own sake; and it is [the view of] Rabbi Shimon, as it is established in the Gemara.

Rashi on Shabbat 107a:5:7.hebrew: חיה ועוף שברשותו - פטור אם צדן, שהרי ניצודין ועומדין:
Rashi on Shabbat 107a:5:7.english: Wild animals or birds that are in his possession - [He is] exempt if he traps them, for they are already trapped.

Rashi on Shabbat 107a:5:8.english: And one who wounds them is liable - For they have skin.

Rashi on Shabbat 107a:6:1.hebrew: שמונה שרצים יש להן עורות - ופליג אדרבנן, דאמרי בהעור והרוטב: האנקה, הכח, והלטאה, והחומט — עורותיהן מטמאין בכעדשה כבשרן. אלמא, הני ארבעה לית להו עור:
Rashi on Shabbat 107a:6:1.english: The eight creeping animals have skins - And he disagrees with the Rabbis, who say in [the chapter] Ha'or Veharotav: [With regard to] the anakah, the koach, the leta'ah, and the chomet, their skins transmit impurity in [the measure of] a lentil's bulk, like their flesh. Thus, these four do not have [a distinct] skin.

Rashi on Shabbat 107a:6:2.hebrew: אלה הטמאים - בתר "והאנקה והכח" כתיב, ודרשינן ה' יתירה ד"הטמאים" לרבות שעורותיהן כבשרן; וכתיב "אלה" למעוטי הנך דקרא קמא — החולד והעכבר והצב:
Rashi on Shabbat 107a:6:2.english: These are the impure ones - [This] is written after "and the ferret and the land-crocodile" [Leviticus 11:30], and we expound the superfluous [letter] hei of "ha-teme'im" ["the impure ones"] to include [the rule] that their skins are like their flesh; and "these" is written to exclude those [listed] in the first verse [Leviticus 11:29] — the weasel, the mouse, and the toad.

Rashi on Shabbat 107a:6:3.english: Even the Rabbis concede - that they have skin.

Tosafot on Shabbat 107a:3:1.hebrew: וממאי דפטור ומותר דתנן מחט של יד ליטול בה את הקוץ - למאי דמסיק בריש פ' הנחנקין (סנהדרין דף פה.) דאתיא כר"ש — אתי שפיר, דמיירי אפילו ודאי חביל, ומשום שאינה צריכה לגופה שרי. אבל לפי מאי דפריך התם: "והא דתנן מחט של יד ליטול בה את הקוץ, ליחוש דילמא חביל?" — לא פשיט הכא מיניה שפיר, דבמפיס מורסא דודאי עושה פתח, שמא יהא אסור. ואומר ר"י דאפילו למאי דס"ד התם, פשיט שפיר; דמסתבר דככולי עלמא אתיא, אפילו כר' יהודה. וכיון דרבי יהודה — דאסר בעלמא דבר שאין מתכוין אפילו אינו פסיק רישיה — שרי הכא משום צערא דגופא, לר"ש נמי במפיס מורסא דהוי מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה, שרי לכתחילה מהאי טעמא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 107a:3:1.english: And from what [source do we conclude] that one is exempt and [it is] permitted? As we learned [in a Mishnah]: A hand needle [may be moved] to remove a thorn. - According to what [the Gemara] concludes at the beginning of the chapter HaNechekin (Sanhedrin 85a), that [this Mishnah] follows Rabbi Shimon — it works well, for [the Mishnah] is speaking even [of a case where] he definitely wounds [and draws blood], and because [it is a melakhah] that is not needed for its own sake, it is permitted. However, according to what [the Gemara] objects there: "But regarding that which we learned [in a Mishnah]: A hand needle [may be moved] to remove a thorn — let us be concerned lest he wound [and draw blood]?" — [the Gemara] here cannot resolve [the issue] well from it, for in [the case of] one who lances an abscess, where he definitely makes an opening, perhaps it would be prohibited. And Rabbi Yitzchak says that even according to what [the Gemara] initially thought there, it resolves [it] well; for it stands to reason that [the Mishnah] follows everyone, even Rabbi Yehudah. And since Rabbi Yehudah — who elsewhere prohibits an unintentional act even [when] it is not an inevitable consequence (pesik reishei) — permits [it] here because of physical pain, for Rabbi Shimon as well, in [the case of] one who lances an abscess, which is a melakhah not needed for its own sake, it is permitted ab initio for this reason.

Tosafot on Shabbat 107a:5:1.hebrew: שמנה שרצים החובל בהן חייב - לשון שפי' הקונטר' משום נטילת נשמה עיקר, כדפי' בפרק כלל גדול (לעיל שבת דף עה.):
Tosafot on Shabbat 107a:5:1.english: [Regarding] the eight creeping animals: one who wounds them is liable - The wording that Rashi explained — [that the liability is] due to taking a life — is the primary [explanation], as [we] explained in the chapter [entitled] Kelal Gadol (above, Shabbat 75a).

Tosafot on Shabbat 107a:5:2.hebrew: הצדן לצורך חייב - וא"ת: מ"ש דאיצטריך הכא למיתני טפי "הצדן לצורך חייב" — בכל חיובי דשבת נמי לא מחייב ר"ש אלא לצורך? ואומר ר"י, דלהכי תנא ליה הכא לאשמעינן דבשאר שקצים ורמשים שאין להן עור צריך שיתכוין לשום צורך, דסתמיה לאו לצורך קיימי; אבל בשמונה שרצים דרישא דיש להם עור, סתמייהו ניצודין לצורך עורן, להכי תני "צדן" בהדי "חובל", דמחייב נמי משום עור:
Tosafot on Shabbat 107a:5:2.english: One who traps them for a need is liable - And if you will say: What is different [here] that it was necessary to teach here specifically "one who traps them for a need is liable" — in all liabilities of Shabbat as well, Rabbi Shimon only holds [one] liable when [it is done] for a need? And Rabbi Yitzchak says that it was for this reason that [the Tanna] taught it here, to inform us that with regard to other abominations and crawling things, which do not have a hide, one must intend [the trapping] for some need, because ordinarily they are not [trapped] for a need; whereas with regard to the eight creeping animals of the first clause, which have a hide, ordinarily they are trapped for the sake of their hide — therefore [the Tanna] taught "one who traps them" alongside "one who wounds [them]," which is also liable on account of [their] hide.

Tosafot on Shabbat 107a:5:3.hebrew: שלא לצורך פטור - פירש רש"י דאין במינו ניצוד. ואינו נראה, דהא מאן דפטר אין במינו ניצוד פוטר אפילו לצורך. אלא יש לפרש דאפילו במינו ניצוד פטור, משום דהויא מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה. ור"ת מחקו מן הפירושים:
Tosafot on Shabbat 107a:5:3.english: [One who traps them] for no need is exempt - Rashi explained [that this refers to a creature] whose kind is not [normally] trapped. But this does not seem [correct], for the one who exempts [trapping a creature] whose kind is not [normally] trapped exempts [it] even [when trapped] for a need. Rather, one should explain that even [if it is a creature] whose kind is [normally] trapped, he is exempt because it is a labor not needed for its own sake. And Rabbeinu Tam erased it from the commentaries.

Tosafot on Shabbat 107a:6:1.hebrew: אמר שמואל ר' יוחנן בן נורי היא דאמר שמונה שרצים יש להם עור - תימה לר"י: דע"כ לא פליגי רבנן עליה דרבי יוחנן אלא לענין טומאה, אבל בשבת דילמא מודו ליה! דהא עור של עגל הרך הוי כבשר לענין טומאה, והחובל בו בשבת חייב; וכן עור של עוף מסתמא הוי כבשר, שרך הוא, ותנן: "חיה ועוף שברשותו — החובל בהן חייב"! וי"ל: דעור של עגל הרך ושל עוף, אע"ג דחשיב עור, הוי כבשר לענין טומאה משום דרכיכין וראוין לאכילה; אבל עור ח' שרצים, סבר שמואל דטעמא דרבנן דחשיבי ליה כבשר משום דאזלי בתר גישתא, כדמפרש בהעור והרוטב (חולין דף קכב:), ולא משום רכיכות, דלא רכיך כולי האי, וכיון דלית להו ממשות עור, החובל בהן פטור כמו בשאר שקצים ורמשים:
Tosafot on Shabbat 107a:6:1.english: Shmuel said: It is Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri, who says that the eight creeping animals have skins - This is puzzling to the Ri: For [why not say that] the Rabbis only disagree with Rabbi Yoḥanan with regard to impurity, whereas regarding Shabbat perhaps they agree with him? For the skin of a tender calf is [considered] like flesh with regard to impurity, yet one who wounds it on Shabbat is liable; and similarly, the skin of a bird is presumably [considered] like flesh [for impurity], since it is soft, and [yet] we learned [in our mishna]: "A wild animal or a bird in one's possession — one who wounds them is liable"! And one can answer: The skin of a tender calf and of a bird, even though it is considered [true] skin, is [treated] like flesh with regard to impurity because they are soft and fit for eating. However, [regarding] the skin of the eight creeping animals, Shmuel holds that the Rabbis' reason for considering it like flesh is because they go by touch [whether the skin feels substantial], as explained in [chapter] HaOr VeHaRotev (Chullin 122b), and not because of softness, for it is not that soft; and since they have no substantiality of skin, one who wounds them is exempt, just as with other creeping things and crawling creatures.

Tosafot on Shabbat 107a:6:2.hebrew: ע"כ לא פליגי רבנן אלא לענין טומאה דכתיב אלה הטמאים - וא"ת: והא מסקינן בפ' העור והרוטב (שם) דבגישתא קמיפלגי, ופי' בקונט' התם דרבנן לא דרשי "הטמאים"? ואיכא למימר דרב דהכא לטעמיה, דתני התם "תנשמת" ולא אזיל בתר גישתא; ומיהו בלאו הכי א"א לומר התם כדפי' הקונטרס, דאמאי איצטריך למימר התם "רב תנא הוא ופליג"? והא ע"כ ברייתא דדריש "הטמאים" קיימא כרב! ע"כ נראה דרבנן דמתני' דהתם נמי אית להו דרשה ד"הטמאים", אבל לית להו "למינהו" הפסיק הענין, וכתב "הטמאים" לרבות ו"אלה" למעט, ומוקמינן ריבויא אהנהו ארבע דלית להו גישתא: האנקה והכח והלטאה והחומט; ורב מרבה כל הנהו דכתיב בתר "למינהו", וגם תנשמת בכלל. וקצת קשה: דאמרינן לקמן "מאן ת"ק? רבי יהודה, דאזיל בתר גישתא" — והא רבנן נמי אזלו בתר גישתא ואפילו הכי דרשי "הטמאים", וה"נ נימא לרבי יהודה! וא"כ נמי נימא: עד כאן לא פליג רבי יהודה אלא לענין טומאה דכתיב "הטמאים", אבל לענין שבת מודה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 107a:6:2.english: "The Rabbis disagree only with regard to the matter of impurity, as it is written: 'Those are [for you] the impure'" - And if you will say: But we conclude in the chapter HaOr VeHaRotev (there) that they disagree regarding gishta [the feel/texture of the skin], and Rashi explained there that the Rabbis do not expound "hateme'im" ["the impure"]? One could say that Rav here follows his own reasoning, for he teaches "tinshemet" [in the list] there and does not go after gishta; however, even without this, it is impossible to say there as Rashi explained, for why was it necessary to say there, "Rav is a tanna and disagrees"? Surely perforce the baraita that expounds "hateme'im" accords with Rav! Therefore, it appears that the Rabbis of the Mishnah there also hold of the exposition of "hateme'im," except that they do not hold that "lemineihu" ["after its kind"] interrupted the subject; rather, [Scripture] wrote "hateme'im" to include and "eileh" ["these"] to exclude, and we apply the inclusion to those four that do not have gishta: the anakah, the koach, the leta'ah, and the chomet; whereas Rav includes all those that are written after "lemineihu," and the tinshemet is also included. And it is somewhat difficult: for we say further on, "Who is the first Tanna? Rabbi Yehudah, who goes after gishta" — but the Rabbis also go after gishta and even so they expound "hateme'im," so we could likewise say this for Rabbi Yehudah! And if so, we could also say: Rabbi Yehudah disagrees only with regard to impurity, where "hateme'im" is written, but with regard to Shabbat he concedes.
